1._: [Siman 318 header gloss] “HaMevashel”—Note: Rif wrote that since Raḥa and Ravina dispute R. Eliezer vs. R. Yoḥanan the sandal-maker and halakhah follows the lenient view, therefore halakhah does not follow R. Yoḥanan the sandal-maker; Ra’ash (Bava Kama ch. 7) wonders how this relates to the unrelated sugya. The Vilna Gaon explains Rif: Rif means “only because later Amoraim follow the lenient side in theft-on-Shabbat can we resolve the beraita otherwise needing another answer—so we lack proof that rabbinic opinions follow R. Yoḥanan the sandal-maker.” Even after asking forgiveness the Gaon’s reading seems impossible—Rif explicitly applies that resolution to the Mishnah of theft/slaughter Yom Kippur which parallels Shabbat; if Mishnah followed R. Yoḥanan the sandal-maker one should pasken him especially since stam Mishnah supports him—Ra’ash’s wonder stands: Rif cannot intend the Gaon’s reading. On the substance see Ḥiddushim there at length. — Regarding ḥatzitzah on Shabbat vs. eating: Maharsha’s view vs. Ḥatam Sofer (see prior simanim); presently seems ḥatzitzah permitted Shabbat (support from Berakhot 11a R. Eliezer vs. R. Akiva about Pesah sacrifice timing vs. eating window—half-measures on Shabbat/Yom Tov melakhah unlike food issurim). Extended pilpul about burning nosar less than kezayit on Yom Tov (ties AhShet/Oḥ Tamid); R. Eliezer vs. R. Akiva on “until midnight” vs. “until morning”; distinction destructive burning vs. mitzvah burning; R. Shimon on melakhah she-eina tzricha le-gufa/mekalkel; connection to Berakhot sugya and Pri Megadim citing Levush about rabbinic vs. Torah severity tiers; cross-ref OC §327 and Beitzah 20b shelakot derabanan vs. derasha derabanan; ends with remark to study Levush/Maharsha carefully.
